top_stories.title: Excise crackdown: Over 1,200 cases booked; large quantities of illicit liquor, ganja and drugs seized across Telangana - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Excise officials** in **Telangana** have conducted a statewide crackdown on illicit liquor, resulting in the booking of 1,218 individuals. The operation, involving joint efforts from the **Excise Department**, **State Task Force (STF)**, **District Task Force (DTF)**, **Enforcement teams**, and the **Drugs Control Administration (DCA)**, has led to the seizure of significant quantities of illicit liquor, ganja, and other narcotics.

top_stories.title: CBI arrests Latur-based doctor and Pune Physics teacher in NEET-UG 2026 case - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** arrested two more individuals, **Manoj Shirure**, a Latur-based doctor, and **Tejas Harshadkumar Shah**, a physics faculty at **Dr Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy (APMA)**, in connection with the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.  The arrests bring the total number of individuals apprehended to 13. The CBI is continuing its investigation into the conspiracy and chain of events surrounding the leak.

top_stories.title: Probe incidents of accused being paraded in underwear: APDR writes to West Bengal Human Rights Commission - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: A civil rights organization, the **Association of Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR)**, has filed a complaint with the **West Bengal Human Rights Commission** alleging that police officers in Howrah district paraded two accused individuals in their underwear and vests. The APDR cites two incidents at Golabari and Sankrail police stations on May 24th and 25th respectively, where the accused were subjected to this treatment.  The organization argues that these actions violate human rights and are a form of "criminal force" by law enforcement.

top_stories.title: Rate at which West Bengal tribunals restoring names of deleted electors proves genuine voters not allowed to vote: Prasenjit Bose - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Prasenjit Bose**, chairperson of the SIR Committee of West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, stated that appellate tribunals have restored the names of 4,043 electors (61%) from over 25 lakh appeals against deletions in West Bengal.  He emphasized that this evidence demonstrates how genuine voters were wrongfully deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. **Bose** also pointed out that while the Supreme Court upheld the SIR exercise in Bihar, a clear judicial forum for electors to challenge decisions is necessary. The SIR resulted in 27 lakh voters being excluded from West Bengal electoral rolls on April 7th, weeks before the Assembly polls, with significant deletions occurring in two Muslim-dominated districts.

top_stories.title: Russia to task bankers with shooting down Ukrainian drones | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Russia** has passed a bill allowing trained bank employees to shoot down Ukrainian drones. The legislation, which would see banks install electronic jamming systems and train staff to use them, aims to protect Bank of Russia facilities and other key institutions from drone attacks.  The bill must still be approved by the upper house Federation Council and signed by President **Vladimir Putin** before coming into force.

top_stories.title: Twisha Singh death case: Madhya Pradesh HC quashes anticipatory bail of retired judge Giribala Singh - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Madhya Pradesh High Court** has quashed the anticipatory bail granted to retired Bhopal district judge Giribala Singh in the Twisha Sharma dowry harassment and death case. The court found that the trial court did not consider relevant aspects while granting the bail, and that the respondent, Ms. Singh, had violated the law by making public statements and flouting investigation procedures. The **CBI**, which took over the case from an SIT of the Bhopal Police, also intervened in the petitions and sought the quashing of the local court's order.  The trial court had granted anticipatory bail to Ms. Singh on May 15 after an FIR was lodged by local police.

top_stories.title: India orders demolition drive along border as Pakistan tensions simmer | India-Pakistan Tensions News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **India's** interior minister, Amit Shah, ordered the demolition of buildings within 15km of the border with **Pakistan**, citing the need to address "trans-border crimes" including infiltration and narcotics smuggling.  Shah also directed officials to enforce a zero-tolerance policy against illegal constructions along the border. This action comes amid heightened tensions between the two South Asian neighbors, following last year's deadly conflict in Kashmir.

top_stories.title: US stocks today: Dow posts closing record high, S&P 500, Nasdaq muted as AI rally pauses - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: Banking stocks declined as **JPMorgan Chase** CEO Jamie Dimon warned of increased expenses, while the White House denied reports of Iran restoring Strait of Hormuz shipping. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose, driven by healthcare and consumer stocks, but tech shares fell after reaching record highs. The S&P 500 gained slightly, with energy and chip stocks experiencing declines.  Analysts suggest that market momentum is stretched while the Federal Reserve's key inflation measure will provide further insight into monetary policy.

top_stories.title: India sends emergency medical supplies for Ebola outbreak response in Congo - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **India** has sent emergency pharmaceutical supplies to support the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Congo, as confirmed by the **Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention**. The consignment includes essential diagnostics, therapeutics, infection prevention and control materials, and case management support.  The supplies were received in Uganda by the Eastern Africa Regional Coordinating Centre and will be deployed to affected communities in eastern DR Congo. **The World Health Organization** declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17th.

top_stories.title: Australia politics live: Rishworth says jobseeker changes to address ‘varying quality’ of for-profit job providers | Australia news | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Amanda Rishworth**, the social services minister, defended her decision to keep for-profit aspects of the jobseeker program despite criticism. **eSafety commissioner** stated that investigations into five social media platforms for failing to comply with the under-16s ban are ongoing and she lacks a "fine-issuing button" to address the issue.
